# fastf 3.11.0 — Doom One, and a Windows pass

Nothing about an existing project changes. Every `PROJECT_INFO.md`,
`config.toml` and template works untouched, and no command, flag or file format
was removed.

## Doom One is the default look

The app now draws in **Doom One**, the flagship theme of Doom Emacs, wherever
the terminal draws 24-bit colour. It paints Doom One's dark blue-grey
background under the whole app, a darker shade under dialogs, and uses its
blue, magenta, green, yellow, red and orange for focus, search hits and meaning.

There are four themes now, and `fastf config set theme` or the settings screen
picks one:

| theme | what it is |
|---|---|
| `doom-one` | Doom One on its own background. The default where 24-bit colour is announced. |
| `rich` | The muted slate palette of earlier releases, on the terminal's own background. |
| `ansi` | The terminal's sixteen colours. Still what a terminal that announces no 24-bit colour gets. |
| `mono` | No colour. What `NO_COLOR` gives. |

To keep the earlier look, run `fastf config set theme rich`. The palette is from
doom-themes by Henrik Lissner (MIT), itself after Atom's One Dark.

## Windows

This release comes out of a test pass on Windows 11.

- **No more lag.** The app sent every changed character to the console as a
  separate write, and on Windows each write is slow. In Windows Terminal, a
  first frame took 45 ms and an animation frame up to 117 ms. Each frame is one
  write now: under 1 ms for the first and 7 ms at worst.
- **Windows Terminal is recognised from the Start menu.** Opened from the Start
  menu or a shortcut, fastf runs in Windows Terminal without being told so, and
  drew in plain ASCII and sixteen colours. It now detects Windows Terminal
  either way.
- **Drives from rclone, WinFsp or a RAM disk work.** On a drive that
  `rclone mount` provides (S3, SFTP and others), a Cryptomator vault or an
  ImDisk RAM disk, projects could be created and listed but not changed: todo,
  tag, note, rename, move and delete all failed with "The volume does not
  contain a recognized file system". Every command works there now, in all
  three rclone cache modes.
- A drive-root base shows as `S:\`, not `\\?\S:\` or `S:\\`.
- Help no longer lists Ctrl-Z Suspend, which Windows does not have.

## Fixes

- `fastf show "Cloud One"` finds the folder `Cloud_One`: a space, `_` and `-`
  now match each other in a project name.
- Projects created within the same second list the higher ID first.
